subject: Proposal: staggered retainer + usage collar for Q4 expansion
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@ferris.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@ferris.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + Q4 spike — need options

Soojín — thanks for the plan you sent over yesterday. We reviewed the high-level numbers with finance and product. Two things we need to resolve before we can move to procurement: a firm price hold for the next two quarters (to protect our forecast while we ramp) and a short-term usage collar to handle an expected Q4 traffic spike.

Specifically: can Redwood hold the per-token rate for 2 quarters at the proposed committed tier if we increase the committed capacity by ~25% for Q4 (not permanent)? And can you offer a credit or rebate if usage exceeds the collar threshold so we don't get punitive overage pricing during the spike?

We're happy to sign quickly if we can get an amendment that ties credits to clearly defined milestones (weekly usage cap, post-Q4 true-up). Attaching our internal forecast.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow.

— Elena
Elena Morris
Head of Product, Ferris AI
—
Attachment: ferris_q4_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@ferris.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + Q4 spike — need options

Elena — really appreciate the clarity. I discussed this with finance and pricing (cc'd Marissa and Marcus) and sketched two options so Ferris can choose the operational tradeoff you prefer: 

Option A — Temporal Price Hold + Burst Collar (favored by product teams)
- Commit: +25% capacity for Q4 (three months) with option to revert to original committed level after Q4
- Price: Hold current per-token rate for two quarters (Q4 + Q1)
- Burst collar: Soft threshold at 120% weekly of projected baseline; usage within collar billed at committed rate, above collar triggers a credit schedule (see attached outline)
- Credits: Tiered credit back to Ferris triggered at month-end true-up if average weekly usage exceeds collar by >20%

Option B — Short-term Retainer + Post-Q4 True-up (favored by finance)
- Commit: Short-term retainer that covers the expected spike (fixed fee for Q4 burst capacity)
- Price hold: discounted rate locked for 1 quarter, with an option to extend if target metrics are met
- True-up: Excess usage reconciled after Q4 with credits applied against next invoice

I attached a draft proposal (Ferris_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf) with sample numbers and the credit ladder. If either looks good, we can convert to an amendment and get a DocuSign link. Would you and Samir be available 8/16 9:00am PT for 20 minutes?

Cheers,

— Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing thoughts on Ferris collar request

Quick internal —

I reviewed the numbers in Soojin's draft. We can do Option A but need to protect the unit economics if Ferris's spike becomes persistent. Proposed guardrails:
- Limit the temporal price hold to two quarters only (as requested). After that revert to the committed tier unless Ferris elects a permanent uplift.
- Add an escape clause if average monthly usage stays above +40% of baseline for two consecutive months — automatic re-evaluation and potential reprice to the next tier.
- For credits, use a three-step ladder: 0-10% over collar = no credit, 10-30% = 20% credit on overage, >30% = 35% credit but capped at $X/month.

Marcus — can you confirm whether we should offer the fixed-fee retainer as an alternative? It buys predictability but is operationally messier in billing.

— Marissa
VP, Renewals & Pricing | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morris <elena@ferris.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@ferris.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + Q4 spike — need options

Thanks, Soojin — the call helped. Ferris prefers Option A (Temporal Price Hold + Burst Collar) but would like the ladder tweaked to the following: 0-15% over collar = 10% credit; 15-40% = 25% credit; >40% = 40% credit up to a monthly cap of $75k.

Two asks before procurement:
1) Can Redwood commit to the two-quarter price hold and include the escape clause Marissa suggested?
2) We need the true-up mechanism in the amendment to be automatic (monthly reconciliation) so our billing team can close the PO without manual intervention.

I'll attach a scoped SOW for the Q4 work (Ferris_SOW_Q4.xlsx). If you can incorporate those ladder numbers and automation language, we can sign next week.

— Elena
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@ferris.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + Q4 spike — need options

Elena — got it and thanks for the specifics. Final confirmation from pricing/legal: we can accept Ferris's ladder as modified and commit to the two-quarter price hold with the escape clause (reprice trigger at consecutive months >40%). We will implement monthly automatic true-ups (our billing system will reconcile usage and apply credits per the ladder).

Next steps:
- I'll update the amendment language and send a DocuSign envelope by 8/19 EOD (link will be included).
- Please review the SOW and confirm any scope items that might affect compute patterns so we can model the collar accurately.
- Once signed, we'll schedule an ops alignment call to enable auto-reconciliation (billing & engineering).

DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEF-123456 (will be live 8/19)

Look forward to closing this out — I'll follow up when the envelope is ready.

Best,

— Soojin Lee
